stem.en: Kabir says: "DNA similarity between humans and chimps could just mean they were built to the same plan, like two models of car." What does the pattern of similarity add?

text.en: Cars from one designer share the useful parts and differ freely elsewhere. Species share the useless parts too: the same broken genes, the same silent letters, the same errors, in proportion to their distance. A designer copies what works; only descent copies mistakes.

feedback.en: The plan explanation cannot say why broken, unused stretches of DNA match too. Inherited copying errors can.
Ninety-nine letters in a hundred, over billions of letters, is not chance.

text.en: All living things have nearly the same DNA anyway.

feedback.en: A human and a bacterium share far less than a human and a chimp. The similarity grades with distance, which is the point.

explanation.en: Shared mistakes are the signature of copying. A design would not carry them.
